_doc: Stream E. Zone hooks (PLAN §3.5): ONE memorable thing per zone, never twice in a province, never within 6 zones of itself. `kind`: compositional (built from kit parts + parameters) or bespoke (needs a model, stream F). M1 has one; the ~85 arrive M2-M4.

hooks.name: The Singing Ford
hooks.what: The stepping stones of Fitockpi Ford are hollow; when the river runs fast (after rain) they hum a low chord you can hear 300 m away. Locals cross only in the dry. The brigands chose it because nobody hears them coming over the noise.

parts.line: across the river at the ford

parts.note: a worn carving of a mouth on the far bank

sound.when: weather in [rain] or the hour after

hooks.lore: The stones are humming. It is not a tune, exactly. It is closer to the river clearing its throat.

hooks.name: The Long Stair

at.site: the pass road above Hollin Toll

hooks.what: A thousand stone steps cut straight up the cliff beside the switchbacks by an impatient abbot; quicker than the road, and every hundredth step has a rest bench and a joke carved into it.
hooks.lore: Step four hundred. The carving says: NOT EVEN HALFWAY. KEEP GOING. OR DON'T. I'M A STEP.

hooks.name: The Sleeping Colossus
hooks.what: A stone giant forty metres long lies face-down across the ruins, half buried, the old city built in and around its body. Its hand still holds a broken sword the size of a tower.
hooks.model: A huge prone stone giant (~40 m long, low poly, mossy, cracked), head turned to one side, one arm outstretched holding a snapped tower-sized sword; ruins built against it. Collision for walking along its back.
hooks.lore: The hill has fingers. Very large fingers, each one with a house built on the knuckle.

hooks.name: The Drowned Bells

at.site: the deepest part of the fen

hooks.what: A whole bell tower has sunk into the fen so only its top arch shows; on still nights the bells ring under the water and the wisps gather to listen.
hooks.lore: You hear bells. They are coming from under the water. The frogs have stopped croaking to listen.

hooks.name: The Whale Arch
hooks.what: The ribs of an enormous sea creature stand on the beach as an arch the road passes through; the town hangs lanterns from it on feast days.
hooks.model: Giant whale-like skeleton ribcage (~25 m) half sunk in sand, ribs forming an arch over a road; bleached bone, barnacles near the base; lantern hooks.
hooks.lore: The road goes through the ribs. Nobody in Saltmouth thinks this is strange. Nobody in Saltmouth has been anywhere else.

hooks.name: The Glimmer Seam
hooks.what: A seam of copper ore runs across a whole cliff face in a bright green-gold stripe, and at sunset it lights up like a rope of fire; miners climb it on ropes.
hooks.lore: The cliff has a stripe of green and gold running right across it, like somebody drew a line under the hill.

hooks.name: Halsbridge on the Bridge
hooks.what: The province capital is built on and around a huge old stone bridge over the river; the market fills its span and houses hang off both sides.
hooks.lore: A whole street on a bridge. Shops on both sides, and if you drop a coin, the river keeps it.

hooks.name: The Drifting Isle

at.site: the largest of the Gullwick lakes

hooks.what: A small wooded island that drifts around the lake on a raft of roots, never in the same place two mornings running; the fishers navigate by it.

parts.note: a tiny shrine on the isle

hooks.lore: The island was by the north shore yesterday. Today it is by the south shore. The ducks on it look smug.

hooks.name: The Hollow Oak of Wychwood
hooks.what: An oak so old and so vast that a hermit hamlet lives inside its hollow trunk, with ladders and windows cut into the bark.
hooks.model: A colossal oak (~30 m tall, trunk ~10 m across) with a hollow trunk containing a small hamlet: cut windows, doors, ladders and rope walkways inside the canopy; walkable interior floor.
hooks.lore: There are windows in the tree. There is smoke coming out of the tree. Someone in the tree is cooking sausages.

hooks.name: The Thousand Candles
hooks.what: Pilgrims leave a candle in the grass for every prayer; the whole hillside flickers at night with thousands of small lights.
hooks.lore: A hill covered in candles. Some are new, some are stubs, and one is in a boot for reasons nobody can explain.

hooks.name: Three Mills, One River
hooks.what: Three watermills stand one above the other on a steep stream, each feeding the next, their wheels turning in a chain you can hear across the vale.
hooks.lore: Clack, clack, clack. Clack, clack, clack. Three wheels, one rhythm. The miller says it keeps him calm. It does not keep anyone else calm.

hooks.name: The Carved Cliff

at.site: the red cliff above the frontier road

hooks.what: Every regiment that held Redcliff carved its badge into the red cliff face; hundreds of badges, the oldest worn smooth, the newest still sharp.

parts.note: carved badges set into the cliff

hooks.lore: A cliff covered in carved badges: a stag, a boot, a wheel, a very rude drawing of a goose.

hooks.name: The Thorn Wall

at.site: the border of the warband ground

hooks.what: A wall of black thorn bushes ten metres high, grown on purpose by the warband, runs for a kilometre across the zone; the only gaps are guarded.
hooks.model: A modular segment of a giant black thorn hedge (~10 m tall, 20 m long, tileable), thick twisting branches with huge thorns, a gap variant with a crude gate; collision blocks movement.
hooks.lore: A hedge as tall as a house, every thorn as long as your hand. It is not a natural hedge. It is a statement.

hooks.name: The Mirror Mere
hooks.what: The mere is so still that the far shore's ruined tower appears twice; in the reflection the tower is whole, and lit.

parts.note: the broken tower on the far shore

hooks.lore: Look at the tower. Now look at its reflection. The reflection has a light in the window. The tower does not.

tags.needs: a still lake with a ruin on the far shore

hooks.name: The Gorse That Will Not Burn Out

at.site: the middle of the Gorse March

hooks.what: A stretch of gorse set alight in a border war years ago that still smoulders under the turf; flames lick up at dusk and nobody can put it out.
hooks.lore: The ground is warm. Little flames wink in the gorse, and the smell of smoke never quite goes away.

hooks.name: The Sunken Road
hooks.what: An old paved road sinks deeper and deeper into the earth until it runs through a canyon of its own making, roots knitting a roof overhead.
hooks.model: A modular hollow-way: a paved road in a deep earth cutting (~6 m deep), root-roofed sections with hanging roots, mossy retaining stones; straight, curve and fork pieces.
hooks.lore: The road goes down. And down. Soon the hedges are above your head and the roots make a roof.

hooks.name: The Bell Tree
hooks.what: A single tree hung with hundreds of small bells, one for every traveller who passed safely; the sound changes with the wind.
hooks.lore: A tree full of little bells. When the wind gets up, it sounds like the tree is laughing.

hooks.name: The Kneeling Army
hooks.what: Two hundred stone soldiers kneel in ranks facing a cliff, as if waiting for an order; no one knows who carved them or why they kneel.
hooks.model: A kneeling stone soldier statue (~2 m) in 4 pose variants, weathered and mossy, built for instancing in ranks of 200.
hooks.lore: Rows and rows of stone soldiers, kneeling. Every one of them has a face. Some of them look worried.

hooks.name: The White Flat
hooks.what: A dried-up lake whose bed is pure white salt, with old boats stranded across it in a line where the water left them.

parts.note: boat hull stand-ins until boats exist

hooks.lore: Boats in the middle of a white field, all pointing the same way, as if they are waiting for the water to come back.

hooks.name: The Crow Court
hooks.what: Hundreds of crows meet on a ring of posts on a hilltop every evening and hold what sounds like a very heated argument.
hooks.lore: The crows are arguing again. One of them seems to be in charge. One of them seems to disagree.
